description: ORDER BY scope in GROUPED and WINDOW queries - the path whose unmatched keys resolve per source group - measured cell by cell on a real account. The rejections are COMPILE-time and fire over EMPTY inputs: an invalid qualifier and an unknown name are 'invalid identifier', inside aggregate arguments too and in window queries alike, while a bare FROM column that is neither a group key nor inside an aggregate has its own sentence, '[R.V] is not a valid order by expression'. Legal and value-checked: grouped columns NOT in the SELECT list, aggregates NOT in the SELECT list, output aliases, and expressions over any of these - ORDER BY k + 1, max(v) + 1, and m + 1 over an aggregate's alias. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupedOrderByScopeTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE r (k INTEGER, v INTEGER)
SELECT max(x.v) FROM r AS x GROUP BY x.k ORDER BY r.k
SELECT max(v) FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY nosuch
SELECT k FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY max(nosuch)
CREATE TABLE r (k INTEGER, v INTEGER)
SELECT k, max(v) FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY v

error.messageContains: [R.V] is not a valid order by expression

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE r (k INTEGER, v INTEGER)
SELECT k, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY v) FROM r ORDER BY nosuch
SELECT x.k, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY x.v) FROM r AS x ORDER BY r.v
CREATE TABLE r (k INTEGER, v INTEGER)
SELECT max(v) FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY k
SELECT k FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY max(v) DESC
CREATE TABLE r (k INTEGER, v INTEGER)
SELECT k, max(v) FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY k + 1 DESC
SELECT k FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY max(v) + 1
SELECT k, max(v) AS m FROM r GROUP BY k ORDER BY m + 1 DESC
